A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CoMM dataset and generation benchmark. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–F are readable and support reliable comparison despite pagination changes.

before.justification: v2 reports original dataset-quality measurements, few-shot benchmark results, generation experiments, filtering ablations, DPO results, and a human evaluation of generated content.

after.justification: v3 retains these empirical results and adds human dataset-quality ratings, filtering-component ablations, and quantitative comparisons of training datasets for generation.

M1.justification: The three-part filtering pipeline, image-sequence scoring function, shuffled preference-data construction, and supervised/DPO procedures remain unchanged. Table 12 evaluates existing filtering components without introducing a new method component.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same five CoMM data sources, MMC4 and OBELICS, seven few-shot benchmarks, and four generation tasks. The added appendix studies examine existing datasets and task coverage.

E2.justification: Table 13 adds quantitative comparisons against MMC4- and OBELICS-trained SEED-Llama-14B on Tasks 3 and 4. These datasets appeared elsewhere in v2, including qualitative MMC4 generation comparisons, but this quantitative comparator participation is new. Existing model baselines are retained.

E3.justification: v3 adds a human dataset-quality evaluation with 19 participants evaluating 30 documents each, totaling 570 responses, and 16-shot filtering-component controls. The new Table 13 comparison uses LLM-generated MMC4/OBELICS titles as training question labels. Existing experiments' reported splits, metrics, and training settings are retained.

E4.justification: Beyond v2's threshold sweeps in Tables 7–8, Table 12 compares unfiltered data, individual filtering groups, and combined filtering. Table 9 adds human validation of dataset quality alongside Claude evaluation. These are focused extensions; the earlier generation human study in Table 11 remains unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated training runs, random seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or rater-agreement estimates. The new participant and response counts describe study sampling, without adding uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: v3 adds human quality scores in Table 9, including CoMM's DLP/CPL/ITA scores of 8.32/8.57/8.56, unfiltered and partially filtered results in Table 12, and MMC4/OBELICS generation scores in Table 13. Existing scores are retained; Table 13's CoMM rows repeat Table 3 rather than represent new performance gains.

T1.justification: The image-sequence scoring equation (1) and four task formulations in equations (2)–(5) are unchanged. No new or revised mathematical assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs appear in the appendices.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list, and conclusion retain the claims about CoMM's coherence and alignment, improved in-context learning, four benchmark tasks, and supervised/preference training uses. The appendix additions supply evidence without redefining these contributions.

C2.justification: Appendix B newly interprets the component ablation as showing benefits from the collected data before filtering and further benefits from filtering. Existing discussions of evaluation bias, scaling costs, and DPO's limited benefits for image generation remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Table 13 newly documents generating titles with an LLM to supply MMC4/OBELICS training questions. Appendix B also explains how Table 12's ITA and ImgS groups map to existing filters. Appendix E's hardware, LoRA settings, learning rates, and training budgets, along with project access information, are retained.

R1.justification: The same 45 references and substantive related-work positioning are retained. Changed citation back-references reflect pagination, without adding cited works or revising novelty relationships.

P1.justification: v3 updates affiliations and contact details, adds an acknowledgment, and adds a short filtering-ablation explanation with associated reporting edits. The main scientific prose and organization of Appendices A–F are largely retained.

P2.justification: Table 9 gains paired Claude/human entries, and Tables 12–13 are added. Table 5's caption moves below the table, and text and floats reflow, including the conclusion and appendix material. All ten figures retain their content; there is no substantial visual redesign.

improvement.justification: Compared with v2's model-based dataset-quality checks and threshold studies, v3 adds human quality ratings, explicit filtering-component controls, and quantitative generation comparisons in Tables 9, 12, and 13. These strengthen support for the retained dataset-quality and filtering claims. Brief reporting of the new human study and pseudo-labeling procedure, together with unchanged uncertainty reporting, limits the strength of the additional evidence.
